slides.headline: IL-1 Inhibitors remain the primary choice across lines of therapy but Gamifant secures 13% share driven by pediatrics and the 'Build and Grow’ segment
Gamifant is recognized for strong overall efficacy with efficacy-focused messaging rated most effective, while adoption is limited by access and MD familiarity with treatment
Build & Grow MDs are aware of Gamifant, yet gaps in diagnostic confidence and biomarker use remain as compared to other MDs
MDs rely on conferences, journals, and independent medical websites to learn about MAS, with confidence driven by clear treatment guidelines and diagnostic tools
Recommendations & Key Considerations
Agenda
In Q4’25, ~40% of MDs had top of mind Gamifant awareness, an improvement over last quarter, while aided awareness has remained consistent
Familiarity with the EMERALD trial improved in Q4’25, however ~20% of MDs were still not at all familiar with it
Agenda
MDs reported decreased familiarity for most of the aspects related to the development of onset of MAS, with a significant decline for “diagnostic markers”
Association of MAS with Still’s disease and SLE continue to strengthen; rheumatic disease flares and viral infections were recognized as the top trigger for MAS
50% of MDs recognized, unaided, that the IFN‑γ pathway is a primary immune mechanism involved in the development of MAS
MDs cited cytokine storm as the top immune mechanism involved in the development of MAS, followed by activation of macrophages and T-cells
~75% of MDs recognize the high significance of INF-y and IL-1, along with improved recognition among community MDs, but still trailing Academic MDs
MDs demonstrate high conceptual awareness of IFN-γ's role, yet struggle to articulate the specific signaling cascade
MDs consistently identify IFN-γ as the primary driver of pro-inflammatory cytokine production and hyperinflammation in MAS
Unaidedly, lack of treatment options and diagnosis remain primary hurdles, but the most notable shift is the rapidly growing demand for targeted/cytokine-directed therapies
Journals remain the primary source for MAS education, while reliance on interactive channels like conferences and peer-to-peer discussions saw a notable decline in Q4
Most MD referred to UpToDate Journal and ACR Convergence conference to learn about MAS
Demand for practical support increased in Q4, with webinars (30%) and treatment guidelines (28%) seeing significant growth alongside general treatment information
Treatment guidelines, diagnostic tools and biomarkers would be highly valued by MDs to boost their confidence in treating patients with MAS
Agenda
MDs consider advanced biomarkers and clinical pattern recognition as top identifiers of MAS
Rising CXCL9 utilization signals progress, yet low biomarker adoption in community settings remains a barrier to early diagnosis
Nearly half of MDs identified CXCL9 as a primary tool for detecting IFN-γ activation, assessing disease severity and distinguishing MAS from rheumatic flares
MDs cited cytokine storm as the top immune mechanism involved in the development of MAS
MDs noted that differentiating MAS from underlying disease continues to be top diagnostic challenge along with the lack of a gold-standard diagnostic test
Most MDs were somewhat confident in distinguishing between clinical and subclinical MAS, aligning with the top diagnostic challenge faced when diagnosing MAS
MDs recognize hyperferritinemia, as core indicators of clinical MAS; awareness of elevated CXCL9 levels increased among both Community and Academic MDs
While ferritin and cytopenias remain established core indicators of subclinical MAS, recognition of CXCL9 has seen the most significant growth (+15%) wave-over-wave
Most MDs reported clinical symptoms and clinical deterioration as the primary factor driving decisions to escalate therapy for MAS
MDs prioritize control hyperinflammation and rapid remission in MAS management
Agenda
IL-1 inhibitors dominated in adult first-line treatment for both when receiving for underlying condition as well as for when receiving specifically for MAS
IL-1 dominated first-line of treatment in both adult and pediatric MAS patients who failed high-dose glucocorticoids in the first line
Current and Future Usage Summary
In adults, IL-6 inhibitors lead second-line treatment when treated for underlying condition whereas IL-1 inhibitors lead when treatment was specific for MAS
In pediatric patients, JAK inhibitors lead second-line treatment for underlying condition whereas IL-1 inhibitors lead when treatment was specific for MAS
High‑dose glucocorticoids and IL‑6 inhibitors are commonly utilized as an add‑on second‑line therapy in adults for underlying conditions and for MAS
Among pediatric second‑line MAS patients, high‑dose glucocorticoids was the dominant additional therapy
MDs expect IL-1 and IL-6 inhibitors to be the most prescribed 2L therapies; with anticipated future adult Gamifant usage is ~7% patient share specifically for MAS
In pediatrics, IL-1 inhibitors dominate second-line MAS treatment, while anticipated Gamifant use is limited to underlying conditions rather than MAS
Across adults and pediatrics, Gamifant is primarily administered in inpatient settings in 2L MAS/sHLH, with limited transition to Q2 '25ient care
Agenda
MAS treatment decisions were primarily driven by overall efficacy and survival benefits while latent drivers include availability of Biomarker Testing and Payer plan coverage
Gamifant perceptions improved across all attributes with a significant improvement noticed on survival benefit
Gamifant was rated strongly on most attributes like overall efficacy and key clinical outcomes but lags on safety/tolerability, underlying patient conditions and cost attributes
Payer plan coverage, Internal Approval and treatment familiarity were cited as key barriers to using Gamifant underscoring a need to tackle access barrier
The most significant patient barriers to Gamifant use are driven by payer coverage, procurement hurdles, and out-of-pocket costs
Agenda
MDs find efficacy data, specifically steroid tapering and remission, significantly more motivating and effective than the highly recalled MoA message
MDs rated G8 MoA message “Gamifant target IFNγ” as the most recalled message
SOBI reps achieved perfect ratings for engagement and addressing questions, driving high overall call quality perception
Most MD interactions result in improved perception and increased likelihood to prescribe Gamifant following rep engagement
Agenda
Adult patients account for 81% of the treated population in Q4, up from 73% in the previous quarter
Adults consistently represent the vast majority of patients across early lines of therapy (1L–3L)
Build & Grow MDs primarily use journals, peer to peer discussion, medical conference and CME programs to learn about MAS
While Jakafi remains the most recognized therapy, Tadekinig alfa was the only agent to grow familiarity in Q4
While IL-1 and IFN-γ lead in recognition, perceived importance of IL-18 is rising while IL-6 has declined
IL-1 inhibitors emerged as the most used treatment for HLH/MAS among MDs, with Gamifant accounts for 13% of treated patients.
MDs most often cite complete response rate, overall efficacy, remission rate, and survival benefit as key drivers for selecting Gamifant in MAS
sJIA is the most common underlying condition in pediatric MAS/sHLH, followed by viral infections and pSLE
Payer Plan Coverage and Patient OOP Cost rank as the highest barriers to Gamifant adoption, followed MD Familiarity with treatment
Treatment guidelines and diagnostic tools are key drivers of MAS confidence, with expert opinion representing a community education opportunity
Most MDs used IV fluid and ICU admission as a supportive care measure for non-responsive patients
71% of MDs personally diagnose patients and are directly responsible for making final treatment decisions

in Q4 ’25, Prevymis penetration and share declined among D+/R- pediatric KT patients; driven by decreased use among physicians

More than half of HCPs have both CMV and product-specific protocols for pediatric patients; ~55% of HCPs have Prevymis on formulary, an improvement vs Q2 ‘25, with cost cited as a primary barrier to formulary exclusion
Pediatric Prevymis prophylaxis averages 144 days total, a decrease vs Q2 '25, with 64% of HCPs using less than 200 days due to protocol and risk reassessment factors

Most pediatric patients were initiated Prevymis within 0-4 days post-transplant, while 16% of patients were initiated beyond 7 days; HCPs cite clinical appropriateness and post-operative care priorities as reasons for delay
Appendix – Adult KT
ESRD and hypertension were the most common comorbidities that adult KT patients experienced; 2/3rd of patients initiated on CMV prophylaxis were on their first line therapy
Consistent with Q2 '25, ~70% of D+/R- adult KT patients were perceived to be at extremely high risk, the highest rate among all serotypes
Most HCPs were highly involved in CMV therapy selection, with ~70% mentioning NP/PAs actively prescribing CMV prophylactic therapies, primarily based on physician treatment decisions
NPs and PAs self report a significant role in CMV prophylaxis prescribing, with most indicating they are involved in both initiation and ongoing refills/extensions
Prevymis was prophylactically prescribed highly among the D+/R- adult KT patients as compared to other serotype patients
Half of the HCPs reported Prevymis as treatment choice they have personally prescribed for CMV prophylaxis, trailing only Valcyte; Prevymis usage was lower among NP/PA
Top-of-mind, safety and tolerability were the top drivers to use Prevymis
Unaided, HCPs cited limited access, high costs, and preference for other drugs as the top barriers to Prevymis usage
Better efficacy data as well as better access and coverage were cited as top reasons to increase Prevymis usage in the next 6 months
Consistent with last year, ~20% of HCPs cited high out-of-pocket costs and not in formulary as the main reasons for not increasing Prevymis usage
HCPs primarily initiate Prevymis to adult KT patients 5 days following their kidney transplant, with a quarter of patients being initiated 7 days post-transplant
D+/R- patients receive the longest CMV prophylaxis duration vs other serotypes, with an increase vs Q2 ’25
A quarter of HCPs expect increased Prevymis pellet formulation use in the next 6 months, citing adherence, patient preference, and ease of use
In Q2 ‘25, Prevymis was initiated at similar rates in the outpatient or inpatient settings

HCPs rely equally on Epocrates and Medscape for medical education / patient care info, closely followed by Doximity; ATC remains the top conference to stay up to date on new products / guideline changes
Prior authorizations of Prevymis were managed primarily by nurses, followed by NP/PAs
VGCV Loyalists had lower perceptions of Prevymis on all key and latent drivers when compared to other HCPs
Appendix – Pediatric KT
Pediatric KT patients were evenly split by gender, commonly being aged 6-17, with the majority of patients receiving first-line CMV prophylaxis therapy
In Q4 '25, oral pellets were reported as the most available Prevymis formulation, and had the highest utilization among pediatric patients

One-quarter of HCPs expect increased Prevymis pellet formulation use in pediatric patients over the next 6 months, driven by favorable safety profile, formulary availability and swallowing difficulties with tablets
Most D+/R- pediatric kidney transplant patients were initiated on Prevymis in the inpatient setting, consistent with Q2 ‘25

headlines_first_15: Physicians demonstrated higher Prevymis awareness, performance perceptions, and current and future usage than NP/PAs
Physician Nephs trailed IDs across perceptions, formulary access, HCP penetration and current/future usage
HCPs at KT & HSCT centers had higher Prevymis awareness, stronger efficacy perceptions, and unlike last wave, HCPs at KT & HSCT centers reported higher current and future usage
Prevymis prescribers reported significantly higher access to Prevymis, stronger performance perceptions, and greater future usage intent compared to non-prescribers
Among pediatric KT patients, Prevymis usage was better than Livtencity but trails VGCV, and nearly half of pediatric KT HCPs reported Prevymis formulary access
